title: Towards more general control of diffusion models using Jeffrey Guidance
claim: One distribution-level guidance rule that updates a marginal toward a target generalizes classifier guidance and covers multiple distinct control tasks.
layout: 3 panels: method diagram left, two task panels right, green-versus-red numbers
description: The left side shows the method as a vertical flow. A noisy image x_T goes through x_t and a predicted x0-hat, then to a clean duck image x_0. Next to it, a red p(y) curve shifts to a green target p*(y) with an arrow, and the guidance gradient formula with the p*(y)/p(y) correction term sits below. A dotted box notes that p* is the closest distribution to p with marginal p*(y), and that this generalizes classifier guidance. The right side has three gray rounded panels. Panel 1, embedding guidance, shows heatmaps for model, test data and the Jeffrey-guided output, with FID dropping from 20.13 to 12.91. Panel 2, gender parity, shows bars going from 70/30 to 48/52, two face images, and fairness discrepancy falling from 0.54 to 0.03. Panel 3, decorrelating attributes, shows horizontal bars and Pearson correlation falling from 0.54 to 0.01. Red marks the before values and green marks the Jeffrey values.
caption: Overview of Jeffrey guidance. While classifier guidance targets a single class, our method generalizes this and provides a distributional guidance framework that updates p(y) toward a target p⋆(y), with a correction term added at each diffusion step. This marginal-based framework successfully applies to various tasks, including embedding distribution matching and fairness objectives.
abstract: A key strength of diffusion models lies in their flexibility, since their outputs can be controlled at sampling time through guidance. However, beyond simple cases such as conditional sampling, the target distribution is often left implicit, defined only through a sampling rule or a heuristic energy function. To address this, we propose Jeffrey guidance, a principled framework that extends diffusion-model control to applications beyond what standard guidance can express. It leverages Jeffrey's rule of conditioning to update marginal distributions towards a prescribed target, preserving the conditional structure and minimally perturbing the joint distribution. We first demonstrate Jeffrey guidance by targeting a prescribed embedding distribution. With Inception embeddings as the target, this leads to substantial reductions in FID on both CIFAR-10 and FFHQ. We further apply Jeffrey guidance to fairness on CelebA-HQ, updating an unconditional diffusion model to enforce independence between attributes.
